title: terraform: refactor private deployment state layout + GPU node pools, IAM, networking
author: Diego Morales
description: Context: This PR refactors the Terraform state layout and splits the Private deployment modules to make GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking configuration more composable for on-prem/VPC installs. Motivation: customers provisioning Private clusters (especially GPU-heavy dedicated nodes) were hitting state drift when node pool resources and IAM policies were managed in a single monolithic module; upgrades and partial rollbacks were error prone. Goals: 1) separate GPU node pool lifecycle from control-plane infra, 2) introduce a predictable state layout that supports partial state imports and blue/green upgrades, 3) add IAM role/module boundaries to reduce blast radius when adding permissions, 4) keep the public API stable for existing customers. What changed (high level): - Introduced modules/gpu_node_pool with separate state and lifecycle variables (node_count, machine_type, accelerator, taints, autoscaling) - Split iam/roles.tf into iam/core_roles.tf and iam/gpu_roles.tf and surfaced role attachment module for per-cluster policy bindings - Refactored networking/vpc.tf to make subnet allocation explicit and support cross-project/shared-vpc usecases - Moved backend/state configuration into state/backend.tf with documented import helpers and an example to perform staged state migration - Updated examples/private-deployment to show how to deploy only node pools or only control plane changes - Added terraform plan validation tests and a migration guide Checklist: - [x] Module split implemented - [x] Backwards-compatible inputs kept where possible - [x] Migration helper scripts and doc included - [x] Unit / plan checks added - [x] Reviewer feedback addressed Notes on backward compatibility and migration: The previous monorepo layout used a single state per-cluster. The new layout uses multiple state files (control-plane, compute/gpu, network, iam). A migration guide (examples/private-deployment/MIGRATE_STATE.md) is included with step-by-step terraform state mv commands and a dry-run plan. For most customers this is a one-time operation per-cluster and should be coordinated with maintenance windows.

release_notes: Refactor private terraform modules: split GPU node pools, separate IAM role modules, explicit VPC/subnet layout, and state backend migration helpers. See examples/private-deployment/MIGRATE_STATE.md for migration steps.
notes: This change reduces risk during Private upgrades and makes per-component rollouts possible (eg. scaling GPUs without touching control plane). Operations teams should follow the MIGRATE_STATE guide and run a dry-run plan before applying.
